lines.en: Vera, the bus is twenty minutes late again. It must have broken down somewhere on the high street. Nothing else could explain it.
lines.pt: Vera, o ônibus está vinte minutos atrasado de novo. Deve ter quebrado em algum lugar na rua principal. Nada mais explicaria.

lines.en: Or maybe the driver took another route because of the roadworks. They closed half the road yesterday afternoon, so everything’s a mess.
lines.pt: Ou talvez o motorista tenha pegado outro caminho por causa das obras. Fecharam metade da rua ontem à tarde, então está tudo uma bagunça.

lines.en: That would explain the crowd. Everybody here looks like they’ve been waiting since eight, judging by their faces. Look at that poor man by the sign.
lines.pt: Isso explicaria a multidão. Todo mundo aqui parece estar esperando desde as oito, a julgar pelas caras. Olhe aquele pobre homem perto da placa.

lines.en: Poor guy. He looks like he’s checking the timetable for the tenth time. Maybe he’s afraid he’ll miss his connection at the station.
lines.pt: Coitado. Ele parece estar conferindo a tabela de horários pela décima vez. Talvez tenha medo de perder a conexão na estação.

lines.en: Probably. Did you notice that my brother hasn’t texted me back? He must have overslept again. He’s impossible on Mondays.
lines.pt: Provavelmente. Você reparou que o meu irmão não respondeu minha mensagem? Ele deve ter dormido demais de novo. Ele é impossível nas segundas.

lines.en: Ha, typical! Mine probably caught an earlier bus, because he’s always at his desk by eight. He’s such a morning person.
lines.pt: Ha, típico! O meu provavelmente pegou um ônibus mais cedo, porque ele sempre está na mesa às oito. Ele é muito matutino.

lines.en: Lucky him. Honestly, I could have walked by now. It’s only three miles, and the weather’s not bad today.
lines.pt: Que sorte a dele. Sinceramente, eu já poderia ter ido a pé. São só cinco quilômetros, e o tempo não está ruim hoje.

lines.en: Three miles in these shoes? You’d have blisters before you reached the bridge. Let’s give it ten more minutes.
lines.pt: Cinco quilômetros com estes sapatos? Você teria bolhas antes de chegar à ponte. Vamos dar mais dez minutos.

lines.en: Fine. If nothing comes, I’ll call a taxi. Someone must have phoned the company by now, don’t you think?
lines.pt: Certo. Se nada vier, chamo um táxi. Alguém já deve ter ligado para a empresa a essa altura, não acha?

lines.en: Surely. Oh wait, look! There’s a replacement bus coming around the corner. It’s about time, honestly.
lines.pt: Com certeza. Ah, espere, olhe! Tem um ônibus substituto vindo na esquina. Já era hora, sinceramente.

lines.en: Finally! Let’s grab a seat at the back, and next time, remind me to leave home a full hour before work.
lines.pt: Finalmente! Vamos pegar um assento no fundo, e da próxima vez me lembre de sair de casa uma hora inteira antes do trabalho.

teach.goal: Ponte português → inglês com palavras úteis.
solo: Peça uma frase pessoal com 2 das palavras.

facts.label: Deduções sobre o passado
facts.sub: Quando você quase tem certeza: He must have missed the bus. Evidência no presente, conclusão sobre o passado. Sem to e sempre com o particípio.

facts.label: Deve ter
facts.sub: Use must have + particípio quando você tem quase certeza de algo no passado, a partir de evidências: The road is wet, so it must have rained. É a dedução mais forte sobre o passado.

facts.label: Verbos irregulares
facts.sub: Aprenda os particípios dos verbos mais úteis para deduzir: been, gone, taken, forgotten, broken, missed, caught. Sem o particípio certo a frase fica errada.

compare.br: No Brasil, dizemos “deve ter” para fazer suposições sobre o passado.
compare.us: Em inglês, use must have + particípio para deduções fortes.

pages.title: Mito ou fato? · 1/2

items.s: Must have + participle expresses a strong deduction about the past.
“He must have left” means he may leave tomorrow.

pages.instruction: Decida e explique com suas palavras.

solo: Aluno responde e justifica; você mostra a pista.
group: Cada aluno decide sozinho, depois compare as respostas e peça uma justificativa.
Corrija pela pista do texto, não só dizendo “certo/errado”.
extra90: Peça que cada aluno invente uma pergunta igual para o colega.
answers: Must have + participle expresses a strong deduction about the past. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)
“He must have left” means he may leave tomorrow. → Falso (It is about the past.)
We say “She must have forgot”. → Falso (We need the participle: forgotten.)

pages.title: A late bus in London · 1/3
paragraphs: It is a grey Tuesday in London, and the rush hour has started. Dozens of people wait at the bus stop with umbrellas. Beth knows the timetable of her commute by heart. Today nothing runs on time. Her colleague Dan arrives and looks at the empty road. They try to work out what went wrong.

“Dan, the bus is twenty minutes late again. It must have broken down somewhere on the high street.” says Beth. “Or the driver must have picked another route because of the roadworks. They closed half the road yesterday.” says Dan. “That would explain the crowd. Everybody here must have been waiting since eight, judging by their faces.” says Beth.

items.why: Passado de break down: broke down.

pages.title: Encontre a frase natural

opts: He must have missed the bus.
He must has missed the bus.
items.why: Use must have + participle for deductions about the past.

opts: She must had forgotten her keys.
She must have forgotten her keys.
She must have forgot her keys.
items.why: The participle of forget is forgotten.

opts: They must have to left early.
They must to have left early.
items.why: After must we use the base verb, without to.

opts: It must have broken yesterday it.
It must have been broken yesterday.
items.why: For the past we need must have been or must have broken.
